evidence.decision: Chooses one recognizable concept, foreground/background layers, unmasked art and system-owned effects; on iOS/iPadOS/macOS/watchOS it now prefers a layered Icon Composer file because a bitmap is split into two layers and gets Liquid Glass only on large simple foreground shapes, not text or thin lines, as in the new Icon formats section.
evidence.artifact: Delivers corrected icon artwork or specification, or a scoped review, with an explicit layer and variant inventory checked against the guide's per-platform table.
evidence.transformation: The book-club example turns a pre-rounded screenshot with a temporary 'New' badge and tiny titles into unmasked layers with a simple overlapping-book mark, an opaque background and stable placement across variants; temporary text moves into app content.
evidence.verification: Fails if masking removes the mark, reduction erases it, or focus/lighting changes its intended shape; says Icon Composer or device previews are needed for parallax, material effects and export quality.
evidence.applicability: Platform-qualified: Icon Composer and the bitmap-versus-layered choice apply to iOS/iPadOS/macOS/watchOS, image stacks to tvOS/visionOS; tvOS crop-safe layers, the visionOS hollow-shape caution and watchOS black background are kept.
evidence.handoffs: Routes supporting image formats to Images, in-app glyphs to Icons and brand consistency to Branding.
evidence.distinctiveness: Launcher identity under system masks, layered construction, bitmap segmentation behavior and appearance variants are specific to app icons, not generic image or glyph advice.
